items.detail: The **S&P 500** fell 0.38% to 7,520.93 Tuesday and the Nasdaq dropped 0.74% to 25,065.87, giving back part of Monday's big rally.
items.why: Hotter-than-expected October inflation raised rate-hike fears, and tech was the worst-performing sector.

items.detail: October consumer prices rose **0.4%**, above the 0.3% forecast, and core prices rose 0.3%, which leaves a December Fed hike close to fully priced in.
items.why: Fed Governor Waller said a half-point hike should be considered if core inflation keeps running near 0.3%.

items.detail: **Nvidia** slid another 5.53% to $168.80, extending Monday's drop, and Microsoft briefly passed it as the world's second-most valuable company.
items.why: Investors are still weighing the board's investigation into CEO Jensen Huang, and rising rate fears added to the selling.

items.detail: South Korea's **Kospi** rose about 1.7% to near 5,330 Wednesday afternoon, while the tech-heavy KOSDAQ jumped about 5%, despite Wall Street's slide.
items.why: AI chip stocks such as SK Hynix kept rebounding, while Hong Kong and mainland China fell.

items.detail: After Tuesday's Diwali holiday, the **Sensex** jumped 1,257 points, or 1.55%, to 82,363.95 by late morning Wednesday.
items.why: Lower oil prices and the recovery in global chip stocks improved the outlook for Indian stocks, especially IT.

items.detail: The US **Russell 2000** fell 0.65% to 2,822.39 Tuesday, giving back a small part of Monday's 3% jump.
items.why: Higher odds of a Fed hike lifted borrowing costs, which matter more for smaller companies that rely on loans.

items.detail: **Bitcoin** slipped to about $73,730 after the inflation report, briefly testing its August low, as $724 million of crypto bets were forcibly closed.
items.why: The hot inflation report made rate hikes more likely, and spot bitcoin ETFs lost another $201 million Monday.

items.detail: **Ether** fell 5.2% to about $2,028, closing in on $2,000 and extending this week's slide.
items.why: Ether ETFs lost $184.6 million Monday, their worst day this month, and forced selling of bullish bets followed the inflation report.

items.detail: **Solana** fell more than 6% Tuesday, one of the biggest losers among large coins after the inflation report.
items.why: Solana ETFs had another $31.9 million of outflows over two days, adding to weeks of withdrawals.

items.detail: **Gold** fell 2.5% to $4,035.15 Tuesday, wiping out Monday's rebound above $4,130.
items.why: The hot inflation report lifted the dollar and Treasury yields, which raise the cost of holding gold.

crossCuttingTheme: Hotter October inflation made a December Fed hike near-certain, and the stronger dollar and higher yields hit gold, crypto and US tech; Asian chipmakers and India rallied anyway on cheaper oil.
